name.text: WAT 24.1: Fail Safe or Fail Loud!

questiontext.text:
Goal

Delete a skeleton of four Java design patterns and rebuild the safety interlock controller out of plain Python data.

How this works in Python

This is the capstone. You are building a safety interlock controller, and the answer box already holds a straight Java design written out in Python syntax.

The skeleton carries four Java patterns.

  • An AbstractHandler base class with three subclasses and a successor field, which is Chain of Responsibility.
  • A HandlerRegistry with a getInstance method, which is Singleton.
  • A StateInterface with one class per state, plus an if ladder that picks between them.
  • An accept method taking a visitor, which is Visitor.

Python replaces all four with plain data. Here is each one.

The registry decorator

A dict maps a name to a function, and a decorator factory puts each function in it. The decorator returns the function unchanged, so every handler stays directly callable and directly testable.

HANDLERS: dict[str, Callable[[Reading], bool]] = {}


def handler(name: str) -> Callable[[Callable[[Reading], bool]], Callable[[Reading], bool]]:
    def register(func: Callable[[Reading], bool]) -> Callable[[Reading], bool]:
        HANDLERS[name] = func
        return func
    return register


@handler("pressure")
def check_pressure(reading: Reading) -> bool:
    return reading.value < 90.0

A hand-written dict literal would hold the same three entries. It would also drift the first time somebody adds a handler and forgets the literal. Each function enrols itself instead.

The transition table

An Enum names the states, and auto() gives each member a distinct value you never have to read. Both are from the dunders, dataclasses and enums topic. A dict keyed by a (state, event) tuple then names every legal move. Tuples are hashable, which you met in the dictionaries and sets topic, so they work as dict keys. Every move that is not in the dict is illegal, and the whole specification is readable in one place.

TRANSITIONS = {
    (State.IDLE, "arm"): State.ARMED,
    (State.ARMED, "start"): State.RUNNING,
}

Look the move up with TRANSITIONS[(self.state, action)]. Catch the KeyError and raise your own error from it. The from keyword chains the two, so __cause__ on your exception points at the KeyError underneath. The reader of the traceback sees both.

The formatter

functools.singledispatch replaces Visitor. Decorate a base function, then register one implementation per argument type. Python picks the implementation from the run-time type of the first argument, and no record class needs an accept method.

@singledispatch
def describe(record: object) -> str:
    raise TypeError(f"no formatter for {type(record).__name__}")


@describe.register
def _(record: Reading) -> str:
    return f"reading {record.sensor}={record.value:.1f}"

The registered functions are all named _ on purpose. Nothing calls them by name. singledispatch reads the type annotation on the parameter to know which type each one handles.

The session

The context manager from the context managers topic wraps the run. It journals BEGIN, then COMMIT or ROLLBACK. On a failure it puts the state back where it found it and re-raises. A safety interlock that recovers from a fault in silence is the worst thing this program can do, so the exception must reach the caller.

The audit trail is a frozen dataclass, from the dunders, dataclasses and enums topic. Frozen means assignment to a field raises FrozenInstanceError, so a recorded event cannot be edited after the fact.

The pipeline

The pipeline streams, as in the generators topic. stream is a generator, so it hands over one record at a time and never builds a list. It takes an Iterable, which is anything you can loop over, and returns an Iterator, which is the thing handing those records over. itertools.islice(iterable, n) takes the first n items and then stops asking for more. A hidden test counts how many records the source actually produced. Read more than the report needed and you fail.

Your task

The supplied block at the top of the answer box holds four module-level names, JOURNAL, LOG, RELAY_ATTEMPTS and STRATEGIES. Below them sit two exceptions, the Reading and Alarm dataclasses, the audit and retry decorators from the decorators topic, and a flaky relay_state helper. Leave every line of it alone.

  • Delete every line of the Java skeleton between the two banners. Do not translate it, and let no name from it survive anywhere in your answer.
  • HANDLERS, a dict from a name to a handler function, and handler(name), a decorator factory that stores the function it decorates in HANDLERS under name and hands it back unchanged.
  • Three handler functions, each enrolled through @handler. check_pressure goes in as "pressure" and returns reading.value < 90.0. check_temperature goes in as "temperature" and returns reading.value < 70.0. check_relay goes in as "relay", returns relay_state(reading), and carries @audit("relay") and @retry(3) beneath its @handler("relay") line.
  • State, an Enum with IDLE, ARMED, RUNNING and STOPPED, in that order, each given auto().
  • TRANSITIONS, a dict keyed by a (state, action) tuple, with exactly five entries in this order. IDLE arm ARMED, ARMED start RUNNING, RUNNING trip STOPPED, RUNNING stop STOPPED, STOPPED reset IDLE.
  • transition_table() returns one string per entry, in insertion order, shaped f"{state.name} --{action}--> {target.name}".
  • Event, a frozen dataclass with the string fields at, state and action, in that order.
  • Clock, a runtime-checkable Protocol with one method, now(), returning a string.
  • FixedClock(stamp), whose now() hands back the stamp it was built with. Its default stamp is "2026-03-01T06:00:00".
  • stream(source), a generator yielding one (number, record) pair at a time, numbered from 1.
  • describe(record), built with singledispatch. A Reading gives reading p1=12.0, to one decimal place. An Alarm gives alarm E1. Anything else raises TypeError.
  • best_strategy(strategies) returns the key with the highest value, using max with a key function.
  • Interlock(clock), the one controller class. It stores the clock, starts at State.IDLE, and holds an empty events list.
  • Interlock.fire(action) looks the move up in TRANSITIONS. When there is no such move it raises TransitionError(f"{self.state.name} cannot {action}") chained from the KeyError. Otherwise it moves the state, appends an Event stamped by the clock and naming the state it moved to, and returns that state.
  • Interlock.session(), the context manager wrapping a run. It appends "BEGIN" to JOURNAL on the way in, then "COMMIT" on success. On a failure it puts the state back where it found it, appends "ROLLBACK", and re-raises.
  • Interlock.report(source, limit) returns the first limit records, each shaped f"{number}. {describe(record)}", taken through stream and islice.
  • Interlock.screen(name, reading) looks the handler up in HANDLERS by name and calls it on the reading.

You pass when the printed output matches the expected text character for character.

Rules
  • Write exactly one class statement for the controller. No handler may be a class, and no AbstractHandler, subclass, getInstance or accept may survive anywhere.
  • Let no if or elif decide anything inside Interlock. The registry is the dispatch, the transition table is the specification, and transition_table() prints it to prove it.
  • Enrol every handler through the @handler decorator. A hand-written registry literal fails the check even when its three entries are correct.
  • Stream the pipeline. The laziness probe counts source reads and fails you when the count runs ahead of what the report asked for.
  • Freeze every recorded event. A test that can edit the audit trail afterwards is a failed test.
  • Re-raise on the rollback path. A safety interlock that recovers from a fault in silence hides it until it matters.
  • Annotate every signature you write here. This is the shape of the code you will meet in production, so leave a reader nothing to guess at.
Before you click Check

Write down what you expect each test to print. Then run it. A surprise means your model of Python is wrong, and that is the part worth learning.

AI protocol

AI allowed, on three conditions. Write your plan before you open it. Read every suggestion and reject the ones you did not plan. Type accepted code out yourself rather than pressing Tab.

testcode.text: for row in transition_table(): print(row) print(sorted(HANDLERS)) lock = Interlock(FixedClock()) print(lock.state.name) with lock.session(): lock.fire("arm") lock.fire("start") lock.fire("trip") print(lock.state.name, JOURNAL) for event in lock.events: print(event)

expected.text: IDLE --arm--> ARMED ARMED --start--> RUNNING RUNNING --trip--> STOPPED RUNNING --stop--> STOPPED STOPPED --reset--> IDLE ['pressure', 'relay', 'temperature'] IDLE STOPPED ['BEGIN', 'COMMIT'] Event(at='2026-03-01T06:00:00', state='ARMED', action='arm') Event(at='2026-03-01T06:00:00', state='RUNNING', action='start') Event(at='2026-03-01T06:00:00', state='STOPPED', action='trip')

testcode.text: JOURNAL.clear() lock = Interlock(FixedClock()) lock.fire("arm") try: with lock.session(): lock.fire("start") lock.fire("arm") except TransitionError as exc: print("TransitionError:", exc) print("caused by:", type(exc.__cause__).__name__) print(lock.state.name, JOURNAL, len(lock.events))

expected.text: TransitionError: RUNNING cannot arm caused by: KeyError ARMED ['BEGIN', 'ROLLBACK'] 2

testcode.text:
READS = []
def feed(): for record in [Reading("p1", 12.0), Alarm("E1"), Reading("t1", 68.5), Alarm("E2"), Reading("r1", 3.0)]: READS.append(record) yield record
lock = Interlock(FixedClock()) for line in lock.report(feed(), 2): print(line) print("source reads:", len(READS)) print(best_strategy(STRATEGIES)) print(lock.screen("pressure", Reading("p1", 12.0))) print(lock.screen("temperature", Reading("t1", 98.0))) print(lock.screen("relay", Reading("r1", 3.0))) print(RELAY_ATTEMPTS, LOG)

expected.text: 1. reading p1=12.0 2. alarm E1 source reads: 2 isolate True False True ['r1', 'r1', 'r1'] ['relay: calling check_relay']

testcode.text:
import inspect from dataclasses import FrozenInstanceError, is_dataclass
for gone in ("AbstractHandler", "PressureHandler", "TemperatureHandler", "RelayHandler", "HandlerRegistry", "StateInterface", "IdleState", "RunningState"): assert gone not in globals(), "rule broken: delete the whole hierarchy"
here = Interlock.__module__ for value in list(globals().values()): if isinstance(value, type) and getattr(value, "__module__", "") == here: assert not hasattr(value, "handle"), "rule broken: no handler classes" assert not hasattr(value, "accept"), "rule broken: no accept method"
assert len(HANDLERS) == 3, "rule broken: register exactly three handlers" for name, func in HANDLERS.items(): assert inspect.isfunction(func), "rule broken: every handler is a function" assert "@handler(" in inspect.getsource(func), "rule broken: enrol through the decorator" assert HANDLERS["pressure"] is check_pressure, "rule broken: the decorator returns the function unchanged"
controller = inspect.getsource(Interlock) assert "if " not in controller, "rule broken: no if decides anything" assert "elif " not in controller, "rule broken: no elif decides anything" assert inspect.isgeneratorfunction(stream), "rule broken: stream must be a generator" assert is_dataclass(Event), "rule broken: Event is a dataclass" assert Event.__dataclass_params__.frozen, "rule broken: freeze the audit trail"
reads = []
def feed(): for record in [Reading("a", 1.0), Alarm("X"), Reading("b", 2.0), Alarm("Y")]: reads.append(record) yield record
lock = Interlock(FixedClock("2026-03-01T06:00:00")) print(lock.report(feed(), 1), len(reads)) assert len(reads) == 1, "rule broken: the pipeline must stream"
lock.fire("arm") try: lock.events[0].state = "TAMPERED" raise AssertionError("rule broken: the audit trail must be immutable") except FrozenInstanceError: print("audit trail is immutable")
JOURNAL.clear() raised = False try: with lock.session(): lock.fire("reset") except TransitionError: raised = True assert raised, "rule broken: the rollback path must re-raise" print("rollback re-raised") print(lock.state.name, JOURNAL)

expected.text: ['1. reading a=1.0'] 1 audit trail is immutable rollback re-raised ARMED ['BEGIN', 'ROLLBACK']
